provenance.source: FUJIFILM Product Information Bulletin -- Fujicolor Professional Paper Pro Laser TYPE II (Frontier QL type), Japan market; page index 3 (printed page 4) vector charts 13/14/15, digitized from embedded PDF path geometry
provenance.densitometry_note: ステータスA相当 (Status A equivalent)
provenance.dye_density_kind: spectral reflection density (分光反射濃度)
provenance.sensitivity_definition: reciprocal of the exposure (J/cm2) required to reach density = Dmin + 1.0
provenance.caveat: ※ディープマットは上記特性曲線とは異なります -- the Deep Matte surface does NOT follow these characteristic curves.
provenance.relative_axes: H&D logE and spectral log-sensitivity both have ARBITRARY origins: the datasheet prints only gridline spacings on those axes, no absolute coordinate. Differences are meaningful, absolute values are not.

x_axis.origin_note: The datasheet prints NO absolute log-H coordinate. Its only x numeral, '0.5' at device x=207.5, labels a double-headed arrow spanning device x 197.0..218.9, which snaps to the vertical gridlines at x=196.80 and x=219.66 -- i.e. it states the gridline SPACING of 0.50 decade, not a position. The scale is therefore calibrated from that spacing propagated across all 10 vertical gridlines, and logH=0 is DEFINED at x=196.80 purely by convention. Only DIFFERENCES in logH are meaningful; the absolute offset is unknown.

y_axis.anchor_source: horizontal gridlines, each labelled 0.0..4.0 by the printed numerals -- numerals for values, gridlines for positions

numeral_crosscheck.note: glyph centres are the CROSS-CHECK, not the calibration. They fit ~8x looser than the gridlines and sit systematically off by ~0.02 D -- the '0.0' numeral is nudged a couple of points up off the axis rule. Anchoring on them biases every density.

characteristic_curves.curve_identification: by saturated stroke hue (dominant RGB channel), cross-checked against the coloured legend rules inside the plot. H&D curves carry no spectrum, so peak-wavelength assignment is not applicable here; the R/G/B exposure curves are mapped to dye layers via the spectral evidence of chart 14 -- see layer_mapping.
characteristic_curves.toe_axis_exclusion: The frame rectangle, every vertical and horizontal gridline, the tick rules, the spacing-arrow shaft and the legend swatches are all LTLine/LTRect and are discarded WHOLESALE before any curve is considered, so no axis or tick segment can be concatenated onto a curve toe. Surviving candidates must additionally be stroked in a saturated hue (max(rgb)-min(rgb) > 0.15); every rule on this page is near-neutral ink -- (0,0,0) or (0.133,0.121,0.125) -- and is rejected. D-min is therefore read from curve geometry only, never from the frame floor.
characteristic_curves.densitometry: Status A equivalent (ステータスA相当)
characteristic_curves.caveat: ※ディープマットは上記特性曲線とは異なります -- the Deep Matte surface does NOT follow these characteristic curves.

y_axis.origin_note: 比感度（対数） = RELATIVE log sensitivity. The axis carries a single spacing numeral and no absolute coordinate, so logS=0 is DEFINED at the gridline y=363.02 purely by convention. Only differences -- within a layer and between layers -- are meaningful.

stacked_numeral_verdict.question: does the stacked y numeral of chart 14 read 0.1 or 1.0?
evidence: Text matrix of the glyph run is [0.0, 7.1236, -7.1234, 0.0] -- a +90 deg rotation, so the text advance direction (1,0) maps to device (0,+7.124). Reading order therefore runs UP the page, and sorting the glyphs by ascending device y gives the reading order.
Glyphs by ascending y0: '1'@y0=385.16, '.'@y0=390.51, '0'@y0=392.06 -> '1.0'. Read the other way (down the page, i.e. against the text matrix) it would spell '0.1', which is the 0.1 misreading.

Placement corroborates it: the numeral's centre sits at device y=391.25, the midpoint (420.38) of the double-headed arrow spanning y 363.0..774.0, whose ends snap to the horizontal gridlines at y=363.02 and y=477.74. The numeral therefore labels exactly ONE gridline interval, not the whole axis.
Same idiom as chart 13 on the same page, where the single x numeral '0.5' likewise labels a spacing arrow between two adjacent gridlines. Consistent construction across the two charts.

Magnitude check: 1.0 log unit per 57.36 pt interval spans 3.00 log over the 3 gridline intervals of the frame, which is the normal dynamic range of an RA-4 paper spectral-sensitivity plot. The 0.1 reading would compress the whole family into 0.30 log, which no paper datasheet plots.

spectral_sensitivity.toe_axis_exclusion: Identical rule to chart 13: all LTLine/LTRect frame, gridline and spacing-arrow geometry is dropped before curve selection, and survivors must be stroked in a saturated hue, so near-neutral axis ink cannot contaminate a curve's low-sensitivity tail.

spectral_dye_density.toe_axis_exclusion: Same wholesale LTLine/LTRect drop plus the saturated-hue gate. This chart's frame floor sits essentially at D=0.0, so an axis fragment welded onto a dye tail would read as a spurious zero-density shoulder; excluding the rules by element type prevents that.

cyan.reasoning: H&D curve 'R' is the R-light exposure response; the emulsion peaking at 706.0 nm (in [600,760)) is the red-sensitive layer, which forms cyan dye (peak 641.0 nm).

magenta.reasoning: H&D curve 'G' is the G-light exposure response; the emulsion peaking at 550.0 nm (in [500,600)) is the green-sensitive layer, which forms magenta dye (peak 549.0 nm).

yellow.reasoning: H&D curve 'B' is the B-light exposure response; the emulsion peaking at 479.0 nm (in [380,500)) is the blue-sensitive layer, which forms yellow dye (peak 446.0 nm).
